lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A picture graph key says ♥ = 2. Hearts: 4. How many responses? Sketch a column graph for frequencies 3, 5, 2.

FEEDBACK
8 responses; columns of heights 3, 5, 2 with labelled axes.

WATCH FOR
Ignoring the key (treating every picture as 1) doubles or halves the true totals.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Create one picture graph (with key) and one column graph for the same data (at least 4 categories). Write two sentences a reader could learn from each.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
If ★ = 2 votes and cats have 3 stars, cats have 6 votes. A column to height 6 means frequency 6 when the scale is 1 unit = 1.

TRY FIRST
A picture graph key says ♥ = 2. Hearts: 4. How many responses? Sketch a column graph for frequencies 3, 5, 2.

FEEDBACK
8 responses; columns of heights 3, 5, 2 with labelled axes.
teach_steps.explain:
Picture graphs use symbols (each symbol may stand for 1 or more). Column graphs use bars whose heights show frequencies.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Ignoring the key (treating every picture as 1) doubles or halves the true totals. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
